Commentary.Commentary: So, that is it from this game! A lot at stake in game number 4 too as a win for Bangladesh will mean they will seal the series and a victory for the Kiwis will see them level the scores. That game will be played on the 8th of this month and it will begin at 1600 local (1000 GMT), the build-up though will begin a lot earlier. Do join us for it, till then, take care and goodbye!

New Zealand skipper, Tom Latham, says it was a really good performance and they were able to build important partnerships to get them to a par score and the job that the bowlers did with the new ball was amazing. He adds that he had belief in the middle and lower order to get valuable runs and Tom Blundell and Henry Nicholls did just that, which was helpful. Also adds that he came down the order to keep the left-right combination, which didn't work in this game. He also adds that the spinners have been consistent throughout and they have taken wickets along with being economical. Adds that the wickets are very different from back home and they knew it would be tough and they will keep on getting better and bettter as the tour goes on.

Ajaz Patel, Man of the Match, says as a spinner you thrive on conditions like these and you need to take responsibility and win games for your side. Adds all the bowlers did a good job and the batters before that also put up a good total. Mentions Rachin Ravindra bowled really well and they had discussed about which length is the key and he feels it was a great bowling effort. Informs he did have a good conversation with Daniel Vettori and he got a lot of advice as to which length will be good on this wicket.

Bangladesh skipper, Mahmudullah, says that the bowlers did a good job to restrict the opposition and they started well with the bat but could not capitalize on it. He adds that the middle order has been batting well, apart from this match and the top order did a good job in this game and they will look to learn from this match. Also adds that there is a long way to go in the series and they will look to bounce back in the next match.
TIME FOR THE PRESENTATION!

For the Kiwis, it is the spinners who led the way, actually, it was Ajaz Patel who was the star. A four-fer for him and four huge wickets. Cole McConchie was also really good with a three-fer. The others also did a good job by keeping it tight and building pressure. In the end, it was a really good effort from the visitors.

The start of the second essay though belonged to the hosts as Liton Das and Mohammad Naim got them off to a flier but once the former fell, the procession began. They just kept losing wickets at regular intervals and apart from the opening two only Rahim managed to get into double figures. That just sums up how poor they were with the bat.

A really good win for the Kiwis and they HAVE KEPT THE SERIES ALIVE! That partnership between Tom Blundell and Henry Nicholls has to be the difference. That is what took New Zealand from a position of disaster to something competitive and their bowlers then rose to the occasion.

OUT! CAUGHT! That's it, New Zealand have bowled out Bangladesh. Another slower delivery, on a good length and way outside off. Mustafizur Rahman moves towards it and tries to lift it over long on. Rahman skies it high, towards long on, where the substitute fielder, Doug Bracewell, settles under it to take a fine catch. New Zealand WIN BY 52 RUNS!
Commentary.Howout: c sub Doug Bracewell b Colin de Grandhomme

Commentary.Commentary: Slower delivery, on middle and moving away. Rahman opens his arms to slog it on the leg side but he bottom-edges it past short third man. They get a couple.
Length ball, around off. Rahman looks to cut but gets beaten.
A half tracker, straying down leg. Rahim pulls it straight to deep backward square leg for a run.
Scott Kuggeleijn is walking off! Colin de Grandhomme will be bowling the last over. It was going to be Scott Kuggeleijn but he seems tired and it will be Colin who will bowl the last over.
Length ball, around off. Rahim hops on the back foot and flicks it behind square on the leg side for a run.
Slower length ball, wide outside off. Rahim looks to cut but misses.
Rahman finally gets bat on the ball. Length ball, around off and hit to wide long off for a single.
Another swing and a miss from Mustafizur Rahman.
A quick short ball, on middle stump. Rahman gets beaten comprehensively.
Length ball, around off. Swing and a miss from Rahman.
Slower delivery, full and on middle. Rahim can only manage to hit it straight towards mid on.
Full and around off. Rahman squeezes it out to deep point for a run.
A 144 kph delivery, banged into the pitch on a good length. The ball hurries onto Rahman and he, once again gets hit on the body.
Back of a length, angled into the body. Rahman looks to block by misses and get hit on the ribs.
Mustafizur Rahman is the last man in for Bangladesh.

OUT! CASTLED! Scott Kuggeleijn says, you miss, I hit! Length ball, angled in on middle stump. Nasum Ahmed makes room and looks to slog it towards mid-wicket. Ahmed gets beaten for pace and he can hear the death rattle behind him. Scott Kuggeleijn gets the reward for his hard work as the middle stump flies out of the ground. Just the one wicket remaining now for Bangladesh.
Back of a length, outside off. Rahim dabs it down to third man for one.
Slower length ball, outside off. Rahim guides it to deep backward point for a single.
Very full and on off. Rahim digs it out back to the bowler.
Leg bye! Slower delivery, drifting onto the pads. Ahmed looks to flick but the ball goes off the pads towards deep mid-wicket. They get a leg bye.
Slower delivery, full and on off. Ahmed keeps it out.
Length ball, on top of off. Rahim pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Back of a length and outside off. Rahim taps it back to the bowler.
Nicely flighted by Cole McConchie. This one is bowled outside off and turns away. Ahmed looks to drive but gets comprehensively beaten.
Flighted delivery, on off and played towards covers.
Review time! The finger is raised as New Zealand appeal for an LBW. Mohammad Saifuddin reviews.

OUT! LBW! That's the eighth wicket down for Bangladesh. Cole McConchie loops this one up, full and around off stump. Mohammad Saifuddin looks to push at it but gets beaten by the flight and the ball raps him on the pads. The visitors appeal and the umpires raises his finger. Saifuddin reviews it straightaway but Ball Tracker shows three reds and he has to take the long walk back to the pavilion.
Saifuddin goes for the reverse flick but misses the ball completely.
Slightly shorter and Saifuddin lofts it towards point.
Tossed up, outside off. Mohammad Saifuddin lofts it over the bowler's head and comes back for the second.
Fuller delivery, on the pads. Saifuddin works it to deep mid-wicket for a single. 65 needed off 30 balls. Ajaz Patel ends with 4/16.
A touch short and wide. Mohammad Saifuddin taps it to point off the back foot.
Floated up, on middle. Saifuddin looks to turn it on the leg side but misses it onto the pads. A slight appeal and nothing more.
Patel pulls back the length a bit and bowls it on off. Saifuddin defends it out.
FOUR! Finally a boundary after 70 balls! Tossed up, outside off and Mohammad Saifuddin whacks it back past the bowler and into the fence.
Slower through the air and on off. Saifuddin works it to mid-wicket.
Short and wide, Rahim taps it to point.
Tossed up, outside off. Rahim guides it to short third man.
Flatter delivery, on off. Mohammad Saifuddin punches it off the back foot to long on for a single.
A touch shorter and Rahim pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Flatter ball, outside off. Rahim looks to reverse sweep but misses.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tom Blundell takes a blinder. This one is tossed up, outside off and Nurul Hasan just had to go after it. Hasan hangs back and whacks it towards the long on fence. It sounded good off the bat but it was off the toe end and hence the elevation but not the distance. Tom Blundell makes good ground from long on and takes a brilliant catch diving to his left. Bangladesh are in deep, deep trouble now.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Cole McConchie

Commentary.Commentary: Floated delivery, on the stumps. Hasan works it on the leg side for a single.
Tossed up, on off. Hasan lifts it inside out, over the covers and races back for the second.
Short again and this time Rahim pulls it to long on for a run. Bangladesh need boundaries right now.
Short and wide and again Rahim can't find the gap as he hits it straight to cover.
Flatter delivery, around off. Rahim steers it to short third man.
Full toss, on the pads and Mushfiqur Rahim will feel he missed out on that one. Rahim paddles it straight to short fine leg.
Angled into the pads, it is worked through mid-wicket for one.
Shorter and outside off, Hasan slashes but it goes off the outside edge towards third man for another single. Singles won't harm the Kiwis at the moment.
Leg bye! Angled into the pads, Rahim looks to flick but misses, it hits the pad and rolls on the leg side for one. Leg bye.
Rahim misses out! Shorter and on the body, Rahim looks to pull, it goes off the glove and on the bounce to the keeper. He looked to hit it way too hard.
Full and on middle, Hasan works it through mid-wicket for one.
Outside off, it is guided down to third man for one.
Short ball, around off. Rahim punches it off the back foot through point for a run.

NOT OUT! That was a close call! In the end, it is given in the favor of the batter. A short ball, around off and Rahim works it to short fine leg. Nurul Hasan was halfway down the track when he was sent back. The throw was at the wrong end and Tom Latham underarmed it to the bowler, who finally dislodged the bails. Nurul Hasan put in the desperate dive. It is referred. Replays show that it is way too close to call, even with the zoomer it is actually hard to decide if the bat is over the line or on the line. In the end the benefit of the doubt is given to the batter.

A run out appeal and it is referred! Hasan is walking back! He feels he is short! The umpire is taking his time to decide because it is very close. In the end, he has ruled it in the favor of the batter. Hasan now walks back towards the wicket.
Tossed up, on middle. Hasan pushes it down to long on for one.
Ravindra pulls back the length and bowls it on middle. Rahim hops back and works it to wide long on for a single.
Shorter delivery, outside off. Hasan pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Quicker one, full and around off. Hasan edges it down to backward point.
A single to end! Outside off, it is slapped through covers for one. So another over where Patel has taken two wickets.
BEATEN! Lovely stuff! Slows it up, lands it on off and gets it to turn away. Hasan is beaten as he tries to block.
No Hat-Trick! Not the best of balls though. It is short and outside off, Hasan slaps it but to covers.
Nurul Hasan comes in to face the Hat-Trick delivery.

OUT! TIMBER! Two in two for Patel and he has 4! A first-baller for Afif. This is also an important wicket, Afif Hossain is a lovely timer of the ball, we have seen what he is capable of in the recent series against Australia. New Zealand at the moment, all over Bangladesh. Afif Hossain will be disappointed. Not the best of balls, it is very full and outside off. Afif looks to jam it out but ends up playing down the down the wrong line. It lands, spins back in and hits the off pole. Bangladesh now need a miracle.
Who will come in at number 7? It's going to be Afif Hossain.

OUT! TAKEN! That is a huge, huge wicket! Ajaz Patel gets the Bangladesh skipper and he is amidst a dream spell here. Mahmudullah looks to break the shackles and rightly so, they were going nowhere playing like the way they were, the run rate needed building, he though picks the wrong bowler as Patel has not put a step wrong so far. Mahmudullah makes room as he wants to target the off side. Ajaz Patel bowls it wide and slow. Makes Mahmudullah reach out for it. The batter looks to go over cover but it goes off the toe end straight to Nicholls. Bangladesh in dire straits now.
Commentary.Howout: c Henry Nicholls b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: Rahim's go-to shot comes out! The sweep, it is hit through square leg for one.
Ajaz Patel (2-0-9-2) is back into the attack.
Gets away with another one! Two dots to end a tidy over. Quicker and on middle, Mahmudullah plays it back to the bowler.
Again, shorter, this time quicker, Mahmudullah guides it to point. A dot, dots will only build pressure.
Another one as this is yet again hit through covers. Rachin Ravindra ha been a little too short on the last two balls.
Shorter and outside off, this is slapped through covers for another single. Rotation of strike the key at the moment.
Now the one that comes in with the angle, it is quicker and on off, blocked.
A little too full and outside off, it is hit through covers for one.
A single to end! Goes full and on middle, Rahim works it through mid-wicket for one. End of a long over.
Better! This is quick and outside off, Rahim slashes but is beaten for pace. There is a vast difference in his slower one and the quicker one.

WIDE! Another extra! On a wicket where runs are hard to come by, extras could be vital. Already the second wide in the over. Scott Kuggeleijn needs to bowl with more control. He is drifting it a little too down the leg side, does that again. Wided.
That was quite sharp! A yorker outside off, Mahmudullah looks to jam it out but it goes off the bottom of the bat towards third man for one more.
Angled into the pads, Rahim works it through square leg for one.
WIDE! Gets this one to grip off the surface but lands it on middle. It spins down the leg side. Wided.
Outside off, Mahmudullah is off the mark as he guides it down to third man.
Slower and shorter, takes ages to arrive, Rahim mistimes it towards deep square leg for one.
The skipper, Mahmudullah comes in at number 6. Also, Scott Kuggeleijn is brought into the attack now.

OUT! CHOPPED ON! That's the fourth one down for Bangladesh. Rachin Ravindra flights this one fuller and outside off. Mohammad Naim goes for the cover drive but his feet don't move as he inside-edges it back onto the stumps. Naim was the set batsman out there and he will be disappointed to get out at this moment. Rachin Ravindra once again proves his worth with the ball and New Zealand are in a commanding position now.
Fuller delivery, on middle. Naim works it to mid-wicket.
Short and wide, in fact very wide. Rahim just about reaches it and gets it to deep point for a single.
Slower delivery, on middle and spinning away. Rahim watchfully blocks it out.
Shorter delivery, on the pads. Naim flicks it to deep square leg for one.
Tossed up, on leg stump. Naim clears his front leg and looks to go over mid-wicket but misses and gets hit on the pads.

Brilliant effort from Colin de Grandhomme! Pitched up, on middle and Naim hangs back to hit it back past the bowler. The ball goes towards wide of mid on and Colin de Grandhomme puts in an amazing dive to his right to save the boundary. The batters get a single. Bangladesh are 30/3 at the end of the Powerplay.
Full and wide. Naim opens the face of the bat and plays it to backward point.
Back of a length, around off. Rahim dabs it onto the leg side and sets off for a quick single.
Length again, on middle. Rahim taps it back to the bowler.
Length ball, outside off. Rahim bottom edges it back onto the deck.
Full, outside of. Rahim drives it to covers.
Jacob Duffy is brought back into the attack.
Tossed up, full and on middle. Naim punches it on the bounce to the bowler. That one nearly carried.
Slightly tossed up, on middle. Naim stays solid in defense.
Arm ball, on middle. Naim does well to keep it out.
Flatter and quicker, on off stump. Naim taps it to point.
Floated up, way outside off and tempting the batter. Naim tries to whack it but gets beaten.
Tossed up, around off and driven to wide of long on for a couple.
Slower delivery, on the pads. Naim works it to square leg for a single.
Who will come in to bat now? Mushfiqur Rahim it is.

OUT! CAUGHT! Shakib Al Hasan with a reckless shot. Al Hasan steps out of his crease and doesn't quite get to the pitch of the flighted delivery. Shakib Al Hasan tries to force the big shot and mistimes it straight to long on. Cole McConchie settles under it and takes a fine catch. Ajaz Patel gets two wickets in the over. Bangladesh are in big trouble now.
Commentary.Howout: c Cole McConchie b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Spilled down the leg side and left alone. Wided.
Shakib Al Hasan gives the charge and Patel bowls a slower one. Al Hasan gets beaten in flight and the ball hits him on the gloves.
Who will come in at number 4? It's Shakib Al Hasan.

OUT! CAUGHT! Ajaz Patel has provided the breakthrough. Patel set Hasan up nicely with the flighted deliveries. This one is on a length and on middle. Mahedi Hasan pulls it straight to short mid-wicket, where Henry Nicholls takes a really nice diving catch. New Zealand are getting on top of things now.
Commentary.Howout: c Henry Nicholls b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, outside off and that one turned sharply. Hasan is bamboozled.

Beautifully flighted, outside off and making the batsman come forward. Hasan takes the bait and looks to push at it but gets beaten. Tom Latham whips off the bails in a flash and the umpires go upstairs. Hasan got his foot back in time and he survives.

Umpire review for a stumping. Tom Latham whips the bails off in a flash and convinces the umpire to go upstairs. The replay shows that there is no bat involved and Mahedi Hasan got his foot down in time.
Tossed up, full on middle. Hasan pushes it to long on for a run.
Who will come in next? Mahedi Hasan it is.

OUT! LBW! Liton Das has thrown his wicket away. Cole McConchie pulls back the length a bit and bowls it slower on off stump. The ball is turning in and Das just looks to whack it on the leg side. Das doesn't move his feet and gets trapped plumb in front. Appeal from the bowler and an easy decision for the umpire. Liton Das has to depart and New Zealand get the start they wanted.
Nicely flighted on middle, it was the one that spins the other way. Das looks to go over cover but gets it off the inside half of the bat towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Full again and outside off. Das moves across and sweeps it behind square on the leg side for another boundary.
FOUR! Fuller delivery, on off. Das gets down on one knee and lifts it over backward square leg for a boundary.
Tossed up, on off. Das pushes it to mid off.
Flatter one, angled in on middle and leg. Das hops back and works it through deep mid-wicket for a couple. There is a misfield in the deep which allows the batters to come back for the third.
Floated up, on off. Das watchfully keeps it out.
Tossed up, on off. Das blocks it out.
BEAUTY! Flighted up, on off. This one turns a bit. Das looks to block but gets rapped on the pads. Appeal from the visitors but turned down.
Flatter one, on middle and leg. Das keeps it out on the off side.
FOUR! Short and wide. Easy pickings for Liton Das as he creams it through covers for a boundary.
FOUR! Full and straight. Naim drills it back over the bowler's head for another boundary.
FOUR! Mohammad Naim and Bangladesh are up and running. Short of a length and around off. Naim stands tall and whacks it over mid-wicket for the first boundary of the day.
Pitched up, on off and driven straight to mid off.
Beautifully bowled slower ball. On a length, around off and bamboozles Naim.
Length again, on middle and this one shapes back in. Naim looks to tuck but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Duffy starts with a length ball on off, angling across the left-hander. Mohammad Naim looks to drive but gets beaten.
